steps: Clearances & floor shield

Hold the lettered minimum clearances on the p. 10 drawing (same for residential and mobile home). On a combustible floor, fit a non-combustible floor shield: USA min. 32.75" x 42.5", reaching 16" in front of and 8" either side of the loading door.
Chimney & combustion air

Connect only to a UL 103 Type HT chimney or a code-approved masonry chimney with a flue liner, never one serving another appliance and never to air-distribution ductwork. In air-tight homes, add a fresh-air intake into the room.
Connector & roof penetration

Stove top adaptor, then a direct 6" flue pipe run with every joint fastened by sheet metal screws. Chimney support package at a ceiling, listed wall thimble at a combustible wall; chimney 3 ft above the roof penetration and 2 ft above anything within 10 ft.
Chimney height

Recommended minimum 15 ft stove top to termination at 0 – 1000 ft; use the elevation and elbow table, adding 2.0 ft per 90° elbow, 3.0 ft per "T" and 2 ft per 1.0 ft of horizontal run. One offset (two elbows) max.
Fan kit power (if fitted)
Plug the fan kit's grounded three-prong plug directly into a grounded three-hole receptacle. Never cut the ground prong or route the cord in front of or under the stove.
Mobile home extras
Outside Air Kit plus Fan Kit or Rear Shield Kit, ideally fitted before the stove; roof exit only, double-wall close-clearance pipe, stove fastened to the floor. Never in a sleeping area.

Required for a mobile home (USA) or transportable building (Canada): Outside Air Kit S.Z1726 / S.Z1726B and either Fan Kit S.Z1714 or Rear Shield Kit S.Z4015, installed before the appliance where possible (follow the kits' own instructions).

  • Roof exit only. Flue pipe double-wall, close-clearance type with CAN/ULC-S629 or ULCS610 designation; single wall pipe is not allowed.
  • Prefab chimney: follow its maker's instructions precisely and buy the ceiling support package (fire stops, insulation shield, roof flashing, cap) from the same maker.
  • Fasten the stove to the floor with the tie-downs provided in the Outside Air Kit: Parlor Leg Kit with the S.ZR8039 Leg Anchor Kit; Ultra Pedestal with #10 screws and washers through the two holes in the pedestal base; Classic Base with #10 screws and the shipping brackets from the firebox crate.
  • The fresh-air hose must never penetrate a wall higher than the bottom of the intake air channel on the rear of the stove; it must feed up into the channel.
  • Maintain the structural integrity of the floor, wall and ceiling/roof. Open area only, never a bedroom. The chimney must be removed to transport the building.
Fit the base kit
Install the Parlor Leg, Classic Base or Ultra Pedestal kit before connecting to the chimney. Lean the stove back with cardboard in the firebox to support the bricks.

One of the three base kits must be installed before the appliance is connected to the chimney. Use extreme caution tipping the stove; cardboard inside the firebox supports the bricks.

Parlor Leg Kit S.Z1713 · 3/4" wrench

Lean the stove back onto the main air tube, fasten each leg using the alignment holes and the kit hardware, stand it up and level it with the bolts at the bottom of each leg.

Classic Base Kit S.Z3284 · 7/16" and 3/4" wrench

Thread the two 1/2" x 1/2" bolts in, leaving about 1/4" of thread showing; slide the base slots onto them; snug the two 1/4-20 x 1/2" bolts, then the 1/2" x 1/2" bolts; stand the stove up.

Ultra Pedestal Kit S.Z3903 · 7/16" wrench

Remove the ash channel seal (1/4" nut); thread the four 1/4"-20 button head cap screws halfway into the stove base; take the ash drawer out; hang the pedestal on the screws by its key holes and slide it down; tighten all four, stand the stove up and refit the drawer.
Hang the door
Required door kit S.Z4786: seat the bottom hinge hole on the bottom pin, align the top hole with the top pin, and lower until the hinge surfaces meet. The door is heavy; hold it firmly.

Align the bottom door hinge hole with the bottom firebox hinge pin, lower the door onto it, align the top hinge hole with the top pin, then lower until the door hinge surface contacts the firebox hinge surface.

Satin or gold plated doors: follow the "Plated door & trim care" card in the manual kit.

Never operate the stove with the loading door uninstalled or left open; it can lead to a run-away fire.
First fire
Check every brick is in place and build the fire on the brick, no grate. Curing paint smokes and smells: burn low for several hours with a door or window open.
Installer notes & handover
Fill in dealer, installer, phone, install date and appliance serial number on the last page, and leave the manual with the homeowner.

The cover asks the installer to complete the details on the last page and leave the manual with the homeowner: dealer name and address, installer name, signature and phone, date installed and appliance serial no. The warranty also asks for this installation data sheet to be filled in for warranty and future reference.

Poor draft, gusting downdraft or a tight house → manometer, wind-resistant cap, outside air

items: Improper operation → check thermostat setting and procedure
Wood too green or wet → use seasoned wood
Chimney or cap obstructed → clean the chimney, remove obstructions
Faulty catalytic thermometer → check its calibration
Combustor plugged or not working → clean, test or replace

items: Spark arrestor screen on the cap plugged → clean to bare wire
Chimney too cold → use double wall stove pipe
Not enough vertical rise → 36" before elbows; two 45s instead of a 90
Chimney not drafting → thermostat high, bypass open, door closed, wait 5-10 minutes

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Make sure all the firebricks are in place, and build the fire right on the brick floor. Don't use a grate.

  1. Set the thermostat to High. If you have the fan kit, turn the fan off.
  2. Open the bypass, then open the loading door.
  3. Put 10 balls of non-glossy paper toward the front. Crisscross 20 pieces of kindling on top, leaving air gaps.
  4. Light it and leave the door cracked open. Stay with the stove.
  5. When the kindling is fully burning, add two or three medium logs. Keep the door unlatched until they catch.
  6. Latch the door. When the combustor temperature starts to climb, close the bypass. A door left open after the wood catches can wear out the combustor early.
  7. When nearly all the wood is burning and the thermometer reads Active, open the bypass and door and load the rest, as far back as it goes. Latch the door and close the bypass.
  8. Leave it on High until the fire is well established, then turn the thermostat down gradually.
Very first fire: curing paint gives off a strong smell and some smoke. Burn low for several hours with a door or window open. A color change is normal.
Note: the lighting steps say to turn the fan on high once the door is closed and the combustor is warming, and also to turn it on after the initial warm-up (p. 25); the fan section says to keep it off until the stove reaches normal operating temperature (p. 21).

controls.title: Thermostat, bypass & fan
controls.html:
Thermostat knob

It's on the upper right rear corner. High gives the fastest burn and the most heat; turn it counter clockwise for less. Change it gradually, because a sudden big change can make the thermostat work poorly. Your home, the installation and the weather all affect the burn, so try a few positions.

Turned down too low or too fast, the fire can go out or the thermometer can drop into Inactive. Turn it back up and let the fire re-establish. The lowest burn rate is set at the factory and must not be altered.

Bypass handle

It's on the right side. Pointing forward means the bypass is open and smoke skips the combustor, which you want for lighting and reloading. To close it, rotate the handle clockwise until it points to the rear, then push down until you hear a click.

Fan kit (if fitted)

The fan section says to keep it off until the stove reaches normal operating temperature. About 30 minutes after the fire is established, match fan speed to the thermostat: low with low, medium with medium, high with high. The lighting steps give a different timing; see Light a fire.

thermometer.title: Reading the catalytic thermometer
thermometer.html:
Smoke from the fire passes through the catalytic combustor, which burns it off for a clean, efficient fire. The thermometer on top of the stove reads the exhaust just after the combustor and tells you one thing: is it Active or Inactive?

  • Active: the combustor is working and the burn is clean. Keep the stove here. A healthy combustor stays above 500F and often passes 1000 F.
  • Inactive: below 500F, so not a clean burn. Turn the thermostat up and let the fire re-establish.
Normal: turning the thermostat down, especially early in a burn, can make the combustor temperature climb for up to several hours. That's no concern.

Looking after the combustor

Look it over at least three times each heating season. If the needle won't reach Active, it may need cleaning: with the stove cold, lift off the flame shield and brush the face gently with a soft paint brush, or pass a vacuum near it. Never scrape it. A hot fire is often the best cleaner. Still not Active? The combustor or thermometer may need replacing, so call your Blaze King dealer.

Note: p. 23 says to turn the fan off for about 5 minutes before reading the thermometer; p. 34 and p. 40 say 10 minutes.

reload.title: Reloading the stove
reload.html:
If the thermometer is still in the Active zone, follow these steps. If it has dropped to Inactive, start again with Light a fire.

  1. Have your next load ready. Turn the thermostat to High and wait a few minutes for the air flow to settle.
  2. Open the bypass and wait a few more minutes.
  3. Crack the loading door open to let room air in. Give it about a minute.
  4. Open the door slowly and load. If smoke spills out, close the door a little until the chimney draws again.
  5. Latch the door and close the bypass right away. Leave it on High until the fire is well established, then turn the thermostat down.

On low settings you may see very little flame. That's fine: the needle staying in the Active zone shows the burn is continuing.

Fill it up: don't be afraid to load the stove fully. The wood only burns at the rate the thermostat is set to. Load only within the shaded loading area pictured on p. 24; loading beyond it is a safety hazard and voids the warranty.

When to reload: the thermometer helps, but also watch for little wood left in the firebox or the room cooling down.

wood.title: Choosing firewood
wood.html:
Burn only natural, seasoned cord wood. Dry wood heats your home; wet wood wastes its energy boiling off water and builds up creosote.

  • Aim for 20% moisture or lower: split, stack and keep it covered from rain and snow for at least 24 months, stacked so air reaches all of it.
  • Don't burn wet, green or unseasoned wood. It can cause excessive creosote build-up, and if that ignites it can cause a chimney fire that may result in a house fire and serious bodily harm.
  • Hardwood and softwood both burn well. Denser hardwood burns a little slower and longer.
  • Never burn salt-water driftwood. It corrodes the stove and voids the warranty.
  • Don't burn treated wood, coal, charcoal, colored paper, cardboard, solvents or garbage. Burning these materials may release toxic fumes and/or carbon monoxide, which may result in poisoning.
  • Don't burn flammable fluids such as gasoline, naphtha or engine gel.
  • Never use chemicals or fluids such as gasoline-type lantern fuel, kerosene or charcoal lighter fluid to start or freshen up a fire in the stove. Doing so may lead to over-firing, resulting in a house fire and serious bodily harm.
  • Don't rely on lots of small, very dry pieces, lumber offcuts or pressed logs. Used in excess, they can overheat and damage the firebox.

Check it with a moisture meter

It's the only accurate way to know. Split three random logs from your pile. On each split face, take readings 2" from each end and in the middle, with the pins in line with the grain. Average all the readings.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
The easiest way to keep the glass clean is to run the stove on a high burn for a while after each reload. That drives the moisture out of the new wood, which causes much of the creosote on the glass. Leaving the thermostat higher for 30 minutes to an hour before turning it down for an overnight burn also helps.

Long stretches on a very low setting leave deposits on the glass. Running on High for about 30 minutes burns most of them off.

Cleaning by hand

  • Only when the stove and glass are cool. Never clean hot glass.
  • Use a soft cloth and no abrasive cleaners.
  • Rinse thoroughly with water after any cleaner, or the residue bakes on and is very hard to remove.
Don't strike the glass or slam the door, and don't use the stove if the glass or its gasket is broken. Replace the glass only with 5mm ceramic glass.

The warranty covers thermal breakage only, not glass that has been struck, slammed or cleaned with harsh or abrasive cleaners.

ash.title: Removing ashes
ash.html:
Wood burns best on a bed of ash about 1/2" thick, so don't take it all out. Remove ash whenever it comes within one inch of the door opening.

  1. Wait until the fire is out and the stove is cool to the touch.
  2. Put the ash in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. The fire poker that came with the stove has a hook for lifting out the ash plug.
  3. Set the closed container on a non-combustible floor or on the ground outside, well away from anything that can burn.
  4. Keep the ash in the closed container until every cinder is thoroughly cool before burying or spreading it. Don't put other waste in it.
Never store hot ashes in a garage or basement. They give off carbon monoxide and flammable gases that can suffocate and kill.
End of season: after the last fire, remove all the ash from the firebox and ash drawer. Clean out and inspect the stove for warped or damaged parts before the next season.

chimney.title: Creosote & chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow, cool fires make tar and vapors that condense in the chimney as creosote. If it ignites, it burns extremely hot. Hotter fires leave less creosote.

  • Inspect the flue pipe and chimney regularly through the heating season until you know how often they need cleaning.
  • Have the chimney and the stove cleaned at least once a year, or as often as needed. A professional chimney sweep is recommended.
  • Open the bypass before sweeping so soot and creosote fall into the firebox.

Common causes of a run-away or chimney fire: the wrong fuel or kindling-size pieces, leaving the door or bypass open too long, worn gaskets and creosote build-up.

If a chimney fire starts

  1. Turn the thermostat knob fully counter clockwise and make sure the loading door and bypass are closed.
  2. Call the fire department.
  3. Check the chimney, attic and roof for anything hot enough to catch fire. If needed, use a fire extinguisher or a garden hose.
  4. Don't use the stove again until a certified chimney sweep has confirmed the chimney and flue connector aren't damaged.
Agree on a plan for a chimney fire with everyone at home. Chimney fire damage isn't covered by the warranty.

safety.title: Safety around the stove
safety.html:
• The stove is hot whenever it's burning. Keep children and pets from touching it.
  • Keep anything that can burn, like furniture and clothing, at least 48" from the front. Don't store wood within the clearances or in the space you need for loading and ash removal.
  • Run it with the door closed and open it only to add wood. Never run it with the door off or left open.
  • Don't block the air openings or the space under the stove.
  • Have at least one smoke detector and one carbon monoxide monitor in the room, and a fire extinguisher in a central spot everyone knows. If an alarm sounds, leave the home immediately.

Keep the door seal tight

Don't use the stove if the door gasket is missing or damaged; it can over-fire. To check it, with the stove cold, latch the door on a piece of paper (a dollar bill works) and pull it out. You should feel resistance all the way around the door. If you don't, the door tension needs adjusting.

Signs of over-firing: warped plates and paint burnt off. Over-firing can seriously damage the stove and voids the warranty.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Blaze King's limited warranty covers stoves bought from an authorized dealer and installed in the USA or Canada. It starts on the original owner's purchase date, is for the original purchaser only and can't be transferred.

All parts and materials, incl. paint finish1 year
Fan assemblies, thermostat, door handle steel parts2 years
Stove body and steel firebox components5 years
Catalytic combustor6 years

For parts covered beyond the first year, you pay a share of the then-current retail cost: 20% in year 2, 40% in year 3, 60% in year 4, 80% in year 5. The combustor is free for the first 3 years, then you pay 60%, 70% and 80% in years 4 to 6.

Not covered

  • Gaskets, firebrick and plated-surface tarnish
  • Over-firing, misuse, or not following the manual
  • Salt-water driftwood, treated wood or any fuel but cord wood
  • Glass, except thermal breakage
  • Draft or spillage problems caused by the surroundings
  • Chimney fire damage
Report a problem to your dealer within 30 days of noticing it, with proof of purchase. This is a summary; the full terms are in the PDF.

Fuel may only be loaded inside the usable loading area, which the manual shows as a shaded diagram on p. 24; loading beyond it voids the warranty. Fires are built directly on the firebrick, no grate. Brick set (p. 43): A ×17, B ×2, FT ×2, I ×2, QC ×1, X ×2; the layout itself is a drawing.

specHeat.title: Heat output & emissions
specHeat.html:
Heat output (test conditions)11,358 to 34,434 Btu/hr
Maker's website: Constant Heat Output (High) 36,300 BTU's per hour for 10 hours; Constant Heat Output (Low) 11,974 BTU's per hour for up to 30 hours.
Low burnCO 0.30 g/min · 0.14 g/hr
Med-low burnCO 0.18 g/min · 0.30 g/hr
Med-high burnCO 0.72 g/min · 0.81 g/hr
High burnCO 1.54 g/min · 1.76 g/hr

Certified to the 2020 U.S. EPA particulate emission standards using crib wood (EPA test method 28R, report #F18-420); tested and listed to UL 1482-11 (R2022) and CAN/ULC-S627:2023 by PFS-TECO. Efficiency was determined by the B415.1-10 method and is expressed as HHV, but the manual prints no efficiency figure.

Maker's website: Efficiency 82%; HHV Tested Efficiency 82%.

The minimum low burn rate is factory-set and must not be altered.

specFlue.title: Flue & chimney
specFlue.html:
Flue diameter6" (collar 6" I.D.)
Flue pipe6" diameter, 24 MSG steel; no aluminum or galvanized (p. 10)
Chimney6" listed factory-built for solid fuels, UL-103HT (USA) / CAN/ULC-S629 (CAN), or code-compliant masonry
Mobile home & close clearance6" listed double wall close clearance connector + matching listed factory-built chimney

Never connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance (it also voids the warranty) or to air distribution ductwork. A masonry chimney needs a flue liner (p. 11); Blaze King recommends a stainless steel liner, preferably insulated (p. 13). For freestanding installs, double wall pipe from the stove top adaptor to the ceiling support box is recommended; for wall exits, 3 ft of vertical from the stove top to the elbow, and a pair of 45° elbows rather than one 90° (p. 11).

specChimney.title: Recommended chimney height
specChimney.html:
Minimum recommended chimney height, stove top to termination, for 0 elbows / 2 × 15° / 2 × 30° / 2 × 45°:

0 – 1000 ft15 / 16 / 18 / 19 ft
1000 – 2000 ft15.5 / 16.5 / 18.5 / 19.5 ft
2000 – 3000 ft16 / 17 / 19 / 20 ft
3000 – 4000 ft16.5 / 17.5 / 19.5 / 20.5 ft
4000 – 5000 ft17 / 18 / 20 / 21 ft
5000 – 6000 ft17.5 / 18.5 / 20.5 / 21.5 ft
6000 – 7000 ft18 / 19 / 21 / 22 ft
7000 – 8000 ft18.5 / 19.5 / 21.5 / 22.5 ft

No more than one offset (two elbows). Compensate 2.0 ft for a 90° elbow, 3.0 ft for a "T" section and 2 ft of vertical rise per 1.0 ft of horizontal run; the manual's sea-level example (one 90° elbow, 2.0' horizontal run, one base "T") comes to 24.0 ft. Above the roof: at least 3 ft higher than where it passes through the roof and 2 ft higher than any roof or obstruction within 10 ft horizontally (p. 12). The manual calls these figures guidelines; see Draft performance (p. 11).

Note: the table's elbow allowance raises the 0 – 1000 ft minimum from 15 ft to 19 ft for 2 × 45° elbows, but the notes under it say two 45° elbows equal one 90° elbow and count a 90° elbow as 2.0 ft (both p. 14).

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
The same minimums apply to residential installs (roof or wall exit) and mobile home or transportable building installs (roof exit only), parallel or corner. The manual gives them only as lettered dimensions on its clearance drawing; the text doesn't say which surface each letter measures, so read them against the drawing on p. 10.

A10" (254 mm)
B6" (153 mm)
*C23.5" (597 mm)
*D15.125" (385 mm)
E4" (102 mm)
*F17.125" (435 mm)
J44" (1118 mm)
G3" USA · 8" (203 mm) Canada
H16" (406 mm) USA · 18" Canada
I0" USA · 8" (203 mm) Canada
K18" for single wall pipe in Canada
L17.375" (442 mm)
*12.125" (54 mm) USA · 5.625" (143 mm) Canada
*257.5" (1461 mm) USA · 59.5" (1511 mm) Canada

Asterisk note printed with the table: in Canada, a minimum 18" (450 mm) clearance from single wall pipe is required. Clearances may only be reduced by means approved by the regulatory authority. Mobile home installs also need the Outside Air Kit plus the Fan Kit or Rear Shield Kit. Combustible objects stay at least 48" (1219 mm) from the front (p. 26).

Note: the certification label says the stove is not to be installed in any fireplace (p. 4), while the Alcoves and fireplaces section prohibits alcove or fireplace installs only in Canada and, for the USA, says to adhere to the minimum clearances (p. 15).

specFloor.title: Floor protection
specFloor.html:
No thermal hearth pad is required, but on a combustible floor a non-combustible floor shield must be used.

USA16" out from the front and 8" out from either side of the fuel-loading door
Canada (CSA B365)18" (450 mm) on any side with a door, across the full width plus 8" (200 mm) each side; 8" (200 mm) on other sides
Minimum size, USA32.75" x 42.5" (832 mm x 1080 mm)
Minimum size, Canada43" x 52.5" (1093 x 1334 mm)
Under the chimney connectornon-combustible shield, at least 2" either side

The manual says the shield needs no insulation value but must be listed under UL 1618-2009 (Type 1). Where the stove is less than 8" (200 mm) from a wall, the ember pad need only reach the base of the wall; an ember pad can't sit on carpet unless it is structurally supported. Blaze King doesn't recommend adhesive based vinyl flooring in front of the stove.

specWeight.title: Weights, kits & parts
specWeight.html:
Firebox only368 lb (166.9 kg)
Pedestal kit50 lb (22.7 kg)
Base kit30 lb (13.6 kg)

Shipping weights. Required: door kit S.Z4786 and one base, Parlor Leg Kit S.Z1713, Classic Base Kit S.Z3284 or Ultra Pedestal Kit S.Z3903. Optional: Fan Kit S.Z1714, Leg Ash Drawer Kit S.Z3820, Rear Shield S.Z4015, Fresh Air Kit 3" S.Z1726B or 4" S.Z1726. Included: fire poker and manual kit (warranty cards, catalytic thermometer, bypass handle). Combustor OEM part 115-0556; glass 5mm ceramic (130-0246). Overall dimensions for each base are drawings on pp. 7–9.

specAir.title: Outside air & mobile home
specAir.html:
For a mobile home (USA) or transportable building (Canada):

  • Install an Outside Air Kit (S.Z1726 / S.Z1726B) and either the Fan Kit (S.Z1714) or Rear Shield Kit (S.Z4015), preferably before the stove goes in.
  • Roof exit only. Flue pipe double wall, close clearance type with CAN/ULC-S629 or ULCS610 designation; single wall pipe is not allowed. Chimney: listed factory-built for solid fuels, CAN/ULC-S629 or UL-103HT, ceiling support package from the same maker.
  • Fasten the stove to the floor with the tie-downs provided in the Outside Air Kit (base-specific hardware on p. 16).
  • Maintain the structural integrity of the floor, wall and ceiling/roof. Never in a room used for sleeping.
The fresh-air hose must never penetrate a wall higher than the bottom of the intake air channel on the rear of the stove (it has to feed up into the channel) and must be kept open at all times. In air-tight homes generally, a fresh-air intake into the room is recommended (p. 11).

catalog_mismatches.manual: no efficiency percentage printed; efficiency determined by the B415.1-10 test method and represented as HHV

review.notes: Clearances: the manual gives only lettered values (A-L, *1, *2) keyed to a clearance drawing (p. 10; same table on the label, p. 4). The text never says which surface each letter measures, so the guide transcribes letters and values exactly as printed and sends installers to the drawing; no meanings were inferred. Metric equivalents differ slightly between p. 4 and p. 10 (G, H-Canada and K differ by 1 mm), so those mm values are omitted. Shown only as figures and not transcribed: overall dimensions for each base (pp. 7-9, extraction garbled), usable firebox loading area (p. 24), tested low-burn knob position (p. 27), bypass open/closed positions (p. 23), brick layout drawing (p. 43; counts are text and are given). Warranty: the p. 44 summary is a check-mark grid, so the drawer uses the written terms on pp. 45-47; the grid also lists motors, thermal sensors, catalytic thermometer and bi-metallic thermostat assembly under 2 years, which the p. 45 text does not name. The manual prints no efficiency percentage (only the B415.1-10 / HHV method, p. 21), no burn time, no heating area, no glass view area and no fan electrical rating, so the catalog's efficiency, burn time, heating area and view area could not be checked (the manual gives the firebox door opening instead). Mobile-home tie-downs: p. 16 says to use the tie-downs provided in the Outside Air Kit, then names base-specific hardware (S.ZR8039 Leg Anchor Kit, #10 screws, crate shipping brackets); it is unclear whether these come in the kit. The unit.json doc title says the PDF was not opened, but the full 48-page text was present and was read completely.
